title: Reduce streaming token generation latency: token loop, flush cadence, backpressure
author: Ethan Clarke
description:
Motivation: Streaming token generation p95/p99 latency was a root cause in several small-production regressions and customer reports. We observed excessive per-token flushes and occasional queue buildup inside the token loop when clients stream short responses (1-10 tokens) or when variable batch sizes interact with the flush cadence. This PR makes coordinated runtime changes across the token loop, flush cadence, KV cache access, and scheduling/backpressure logic to reduce tail latency for streaming while preserving throughput for batched workloads.

What this change does (high level):
- Token loop micro-optimizations: reduce allocations per token, inline critical hot paths, and batch metadata writes to shorten the token emission path.
- Flush cadence: introduce adaptive flush windows that group very-short streams into tightly-bounded micro-batches (configurable, default 2ms) to avoid emitting partial tokens too frequently while preventing head-of-line blocking.
- Backpressure and scheduling: add a lightweight per-worker admission control to limit queue growth and prefer low-latency single-token requests when latency-SLO mode is active. This includes a fast-path for single-token flushes and a conservative backoff for long-running requests.
- KV cache access: add read-ahead and a small hot-entry LRU window for the KV cache to eliminate repeated lookups for the same key during token loop churn; relocate some cache bookkeeping off the hot path.
- Continuous batching heuristic tuned: prefer tight batching for multi-token long-running requests but decouple single-token streaming from batch packing so single-token clients avoid waiting for larger batch triggers.

Files touched (summary): see changed_files. Small codegen/diff snippets are included in changed files for clarity (hot-path in token_loop.cpp, scheduler admission control header, and tests).

Checklist:
- [x] Benchmark local perf harness across representative models (gpt-like small and medium)
- [x] Add deterministic unit tests for new backpressure behavior
- [x] Add perf tests that assert p50/p95/p99 streaming latency improvements
- [x] Dogfood on internal staging cluster for 48h
- [x] Feature-flag gated with runtime knob (default on for staging, opt-in for main initially)

Testing & results:
- Microbench: end-to-end streaming p95 reduced by 25-35% across small/medium models for 1-8 token responses. p99 reduced by ~20% in steady-state.
- No measurable regression in aggregate throughput for large-batched workloads (<=2% variance within noise).
- CI: added unit tests and a perf scenario; initial CI flake on benchmarking infra caused 1 rerun.

Risk & rollout:
- Changes are behind a runtime feature flag. Rollout plan: enable on staging for 48h, enable canary on 5% of traffic for 24h, then ramp to 100% if no regressions. If regressions are observed we revert the flag or tune flush window.

Related: ENG-2312 (streaming latency), ENG-2439 (kv-cache hot-path investigation).
